**A sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect Speech. Out of the four given alternatives,**** ****select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct Speech.** 

Raj said, “I am happy to be here this evening.”

options.text: Raj said that he was happy to be there that evening.
Raj was happy to be there this evening.
Raj said he was happy to be there this evening.
Raj says he is happy to be there.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Raj said that he was happy to be there that evening.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in Direct Speech. As per the question we have to change it into **Indirect speech**. 
 
• The process of transformation as follows:
 
 
• 'Said' will not change because the Reporting Verb has no object. 
 
• Comma and inverted commas will be removed. 
 
• The conjunction 'That' will be added.
 
• 'am happy' will be changed into 'was happy'. 
 
• 'this evening' will be changed into 'That evening'. 
 
• **'here' **will be changed into **'there'**
 
 
 
• Therefore, by applying the above rules we find that the correct answer is Option 1. ​

options.text: The tree is cut down by the officer.

__
 
• In Active Voice, a sentence emphasizes the subject, performing an action.
 
• In Passive Voice, a sentence emphasizes the action or the object of the sentence.
 
• **'cuts' **is changed into **'is/are/am + V₃'. 'cut' **remains the same in all the three forms.

Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. 

The purple car parked outside belongs to my neighbour, who is an elderly women.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'is an elderly women'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
 
• Here,** 'is an elderly woman' **should be used instead of** 'is an elderly women'.**
 
• The correction is necessary because the **noun** "neighbour" is **singular**, and as such, requires a **singular subject complement.** "**Women**" is** a plural noun **and does not agree with the singular "**neighbour**."
 
• In the corrected sentence, "**woman**" is used instead of "**women**," which is the correct **singular** form of the noun to agree with "**neighbour**." This correction ensures **grammatical** correctness in the sentence.
 
• It is important to pay attention to **subject-verb agreement** when constructing sentences, as errors can cause confusion and hinder effective **communication**. 
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 4.****
 

Correct Sentence:__** *The purple car parked outside belongs to my neighbour**, who** is an elderly woman.***
